about: PROPOSED, NOT APPROVED. What a part of an approved entry states: for a verbatim extract of his approved wording (a whole sentence of an entry, or the leading clause of one up to its first ';'), which of the entry's covers those words say. His reply filed 22 October 2026, item 4: 'I approve generating abbreviated versions of approved statements for the Coach Overview, provided their meaning remains accurate.' and 'Shortening must not introduce new meanings, omit a condition that changes the essential understanding, or silently turn a qualified rule into an unrestricted one.' No field of approved-coach-wording.json records what a part of an entry states, and nothing in the words decides it mechanically, so it is a reading of his words: recorded here as data, keyed by approved-entry id exactly as the approved wording itself is, and never in code. Every reading below is OUR PROPOSAL for his confirmation (the coordinator's decision of 22 October 2026, stage 3E of the communication BUILD PLAN: the readings the BUILD PLAN's EXPECTED PRESENTATION assumes for its overview sentences 4 and 8). Each cover a reading says a part states is justified by the words of his sentence that state it ('statedBy', an exact substring of that part's words) and, where the entry's own note maps that field to words, by the note's words ('note', an exact substring of the entry's note). A cover not listed is left to the entry said whole in Coach Details. The status stays PROPOSED and the file carries no approvedBy; every extract built on a reading here is labelled for an administrator 'reading PROPOSED, awaiting confirmation', and a coach sees no status. Read by back/src/system/rendering/approved-wording-readings.ts through AUDITS_DIR, so the bundled server finds it in dist/knowledge; build.js copies it. approved-coach-wording.json is not changed by this file.

proposal.by: Claude, implementing stage 3E of the communication BUILD PLAN for his reply filed 22 October 2026
proposal.basis: The coordinator's stage 3E decision (E2): one PROPOSED data file recording what each needed part of an approved entry states, for A01-W1 sentence 1 and A01-W2's leading clause, as the BUILD PLAN's EXPECTED PRESENTATION assumes them (overview sentence 4 'derived from approved: W1, sentence 1 extract' and sentence 8 'derived from approved: W2, leading-clause extract'). The 3B and 3C escalations named these two readings as the ones the overview needs; the cover indexes below were checked against approved-coach-wording.json.

readingShape.entry: the id of an approved entry in approved-coach-wording.json
readingShape.parts: the parts of the entry the reading is of, in order: [{ sentence: <numbered from 1, as an extract's name numbers them: A01-W1:s1 is sentence 1>, part: 'WHOLE_SENTENCE' | 'LEADING_CLAUSE' }]
readingShape.words: those parts' words as the entry holds them (a leading clause closed by its sentence's own end mark), checked against the entry
readingShape.states: [{ coverIndex: <the cover's place in the entry's covers, numbered from 0 as an extract's keeps and leaves number them>, row, element: the cover's row and locator exactly as the entry gives them (checked), statedBy: an exact substring of 'words' that states it, why: our reason, note: an exact substring of the entry's own note where the note maps this field to words, else null }]

readings.words: Building team: Score by carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line.

states.why: The progression condition's scope is the build-out episode, the one scope inside which the building team's scores are credited (the building role's credit bound, B8, which this entry also covers). His sentence opens 'Building team: Score', so the progression it states is a condition of exactly those scores. OUR READING, and the least direct of this record: that the episode ends when the building team loses possession is said by his second sentence and by A01-W3, not by these words.

states.statedBy: carrying the ball beyond the marked line or passing to a teammate who receives it under control beyond the line
states.why: The condition's type, a progression: the ball gets past a reference, carried there or passed to a teammate who receives it there.
Its referent is the target the scoring team attacks; his words place the progression relative to the marked line, beyond which that target lies.
The condition's value, 'beyond', is his word.

The control condition's scope is the build-out episode, read as for the progression's scope above: his sentence states the control as a condition of the building team's scores. OUR READING, with the same limit.
The condition's type, control: his words 'under control'.

states.statedBy: receives it under control beyond the line
states.why: Its referent is arrival at the target the scoring team attacks: the ball received under control beyond the line, inside that target.
The condition's value, controlled on arrival: the teammate receives the ball under control. For the carrying arm the words say control only by 'carrying'; OUR READING.

readings.words: The pressing team also scores by winning the ball inside that zone, provided it genuinely establishes possession.

states.why: Whose score it is: the team holding the pressing role, as the entry's note maps it.
What happens: an in-play change of possession to that team, as the entry's note maps it (the note labels that reading of the trigger its own).
states.note: 'winning the ball' (V29, an in-play change of possession, never a restart awarded to it: OUR READING on A01-R1-V29-1)

states.why: The control it must establish, in his item-2 words, as the entry's note maps it. The contested-touch exclusion (V31) follows the ';' and is left to the entry said whole.
states.note: 'provided it genuinely establishes possession' (V30, his item-2 words)
